title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Subtle model-specific differences (rotary/pos-emb handling in Llama, grouped attention layout in Mistral, Qwen positional indexing and KV cache layout) were causing missed kernel choices and suboptimal KV-cache compaction. This PR instruments model heuristics and adds targeted kernel/scheduler fallbacks, plus tuned quantization-aware adjustments (GQA/MQA) to improve both latency and throughput without changing model outputs.

What this PR does: - Kernel selection: extend kernel_selector to consider model-class hints (llama, mistral, qwen) and sequence-length distribution buckets. New heuristics prefer fused rotary/kv-aware kernels for Llama when rotary dims are multiple-of-64, and select grouped-attention kernels for Mistral when group_size matches model config. - Scheduler: add a short-path scheduler for low-latency single-stream requests that bypasses heavyweight batching when SLOs require it; update continuous-batching policy to use per-model windowing so Mistral/Llama workloads don't starve Qwen streams. - KV cache: compact KV cache layout for Qwen to reduce page faults (store contiguous per-layer per-token blocks) and add a lightweight expiry/eviction hint for long-running sessions which reduces memory pressure on Dedicated nodes. - GQA/MQA tuning: introduce conservative group-quant alignment for GQA variants and a mixed-quant-attention (MQA) path that reduces memory and compute for 4-bit variants while keeping logits within empirical tolerance. Defaults are conservative and opt-in via config flags. - Tests & bench: add deterministic unit tests for kernel selection and KV compaction; add bench scripts for per-model latency/throughput comparisons.

Benchmarks (internal lab GPUs, median of 5 runs): - Llama-70B: 12% median p99 latency reduction on single-stream, 9% throughput gain in steady-state batching workload. - Mistral-34B: 18% throughput improvement at 2048 token window when using grouped-attention kernel. - Qwen-14B: 28% reduction in peak memory use for long sessions; 7% latency improvement due to fewer page faults; end-to-end token cost reduced by ~5% with GQA tuned path. - GQA/MQA: 6-10% speedup on quantized models (4-bit) with parity of top-1 token matches within noise floor of evals.

Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime.feature.model_hints and quant.tuning.gqa_mqa. - Canary rollout to Dedicated cluster pool first (10% of traffic), monitor p99 latency, token cost, and model-output diffs on eval prompt set. - After 72h with no regressions, roll to Hosted API for opt-in customers. Full enablement only after additional safety checks.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel selector heuristics implemented and unit tested. - [x] Scheduler short-path implemented and integration-tested. - [x] KV cache compaction + eviction hints implemented. - [x] GQA/MQA tuning paths added and benchmarked. - [x] Docs: release notes and runtime config docs updated. - [x] Canary plan and metric alerts configured.

Related: ENG-4321 covers the wider runtime kernel refactor; ENG-4330 tracks the GQA/MQA evaluation matrix. Linked perf lab scripts: bench/perf/bench_gqa_mqa.py.
